patch.value: Sim-to-real transfer measurement and gap reporting

A Transfer links a source Environment (the simulator) to a target Environment (deployment, or a harder benchmark) and records the measured per-metric gap for one checkpoint. transfer gap reports the gap series across a run's checkpoints, which surfaces the actual failure mode of a sim-heavy programme: sim performance improving while transfer stalls. Because a Transfer depends on both environments, invalidate already covers it.

A Transfer depends on both environment versions and the checkpoint; gap reports a per-metric series over checkpoints in order; a transfer measured against a superseded environment version is reported as stale rather than plotted

value.author: pi-agent
value.text:
Implemented sim-to-real transfer measurement and gap reporting, to every acceptance criterion.

- A Transfer depends on BOTH environment versions and the checkpoint: `pm rl transfer record` creates typed dependency edges to the simulator-side environment, the deployment-side environment, and its source run, stores the checkpoint as the item's fixed_version and in the immutable body spec, and re-verifies both environments against their content identities at write time (environment_was_mutated propagates). A degenerate same-environment "gap" is refused (degenerate_transfer), and an unmeasurable gap set - empty, duplicated metric, non-finite value - is refused at record time (invalid_transfer_gaps).
- `pm rl transfer gap <run>` reports a per-metric series over checkpoints in order: transfers are ordered by recording instant (item id tie-break within one instant), and each plotted transfer names its checkpoint and every measured gap; per-metric series are aligned across transfers, with a missing measurement shown as an explicit NaN hole rather than silently shifting the series.
- A transfer measured against a superseded environment version is reported as STALE rather than plotted: either side's environment failing the invalidation check (edited, unreadable, no recorded identity, unresolvable) holds the whole transfer out of every series with its reason stated - half of a broken measurement is still broken. The report also refuses unreadable hand-authored bodies (transfer_unreadable), skips id-less list rows, filters other runs' transfers, and reports an empty series honestly.

Measured gates this session: npm test 226/226 pass; npm run coverage - 16 source file(s) at 100/100/100 lines/branches/functions, thresholds met; npm run docstring - 16 file(s), 116 declaration(s) documented; typecheck, lint, jscpd duplicates green.

Revert-proof verification: each refusal/guard was temporarily reverted and its pinned test confirmed to FAIL, then restored from git: degenerate_transfer, the stale-exclusion guard (reverted to plot stale transfers; the test caught it), transfer_unreadable, and the record-time environment identity verification.

patch.value: All acceptance criteria met: a Transfer depends on both environment versions and the checkpoint through typed edges (verified against content identities at write); transfer gap reports a per-metric series over checkpoints in recording order with aligned metrics; a transfer measured against a superseded environment version is reported stale with its reason rather than plotted. Gates: 226/226 tests, coverage 100/100/100 across 16 files, docstring 116 declarations, lint/duplicates/typecheck green. Four refusal paths verified revert-proof.

Review-follow-up (PR 16 round 3): closure evidence now cites the exact regression tests in test/transfer.test.ts that pin this feature's behaviour:

- Dependency edges, write-time environment re-verification and record-time refusals: "recording links both environment versions, the run and the checkpoint; refusals fail closed".
- Ordered per-metric series and stale-transfer exclusion: "gap reports the per-metric series across checkpoints in order and marks superseded transfers stale".
- Id-less row skipping, transfer_unreadable refusal, and other-run filtering: "the gap skips id-less rows, refuses unreadable transfers, and filters other runs' transfers".
- New this round: "gap metrics canonicalize in byte order, independent of host locale" pins the locale-independent gap ordering that feeds the content-addressed body hash.
